draft.title: Comparing ideas across a text
card: A strong text response follows one idea from the start of a text to the end. It does not stay inside a single scene.
Develops
the idea grows deeper or clearer as the text goes on, such as a character's guilt becoming harder to hide.
Shifts
the idea changes direction, such as trust turning into suspicion.
Contrasts
two parts of the text treat the idea in opposite ways, such as an early scene of safety set against a late scene of danger.
draft.remember: Follow one idea from start to end and show how it changes or contrasts.

a.q: Which sentence from an essay best compares an idea across a text?
opts: At first Mara trusts the town, but by the end she fears it
In the first chapter, Mara describes the town as friendly
Mara is the main character and tells the story herself
The town is described in detail by Mara in chapter one
a.why: The first sentence links an early view of the town to a later one, so it shows the idea shifting. The others stay in one place or describe the text without tracing any change. The second is tempting, but it only covers one chapter.
a.clue: Look for the sentence that links the start to the end.

b.q: In an invented novel, Tom's father praises hard work in chapter two. In chapter nine, the same work leaves him exhausted and unwell. Which approach compares the idea best?
opts: Set the praise of work in chapter two against its cost later
Explain closely how Tom's father speaks about work early on
Argue that chapter nine matters more than chapter two does
List every mention of work in the novel in the order it appears
b.why: The best approach sets the early praise against the later cost, which is a contrast across the text. Explaining only chapter two stays in one scene, and listing every mention gathers material without showing how the idea changes.
b.clue: Which choice puts two parts of the text side by side?
